faqs.a: No. Google measures in pixels, not characters, and wide letters (W, M) take more room than narrow ones (i, l). The character count is a handy proxy, but the pixel estimate is the more honest signal. This tool shows both.
Google truncates it with an ellipsis (...). The cut-off part still exists on your page but searchers never see it, so your most important words should sit in the first 60 characters.
faqs.q: What happens if my title is too long?

faqs.a: A good title is 50-60 characters, includes your main keyword near the front, and reads like a human wrote it. Avoid stuffing keywords or repeating your brand on every page.
faqs.q: What makes a good meta title?

faqs.a: A good description is 140-155 characters, summarises the page in one or two sentences, and includes a reason to click. It does not directly raise rankings, but a better snippet earns more clicks.
faqs.q: What makes a good meta description?

faqs.a: It is a rough estimate: characters x 8 px for titles, x 7 px for descriptions. Real rendering depends on the actual letters and the visitor's device. Treat it as a guide, not a measurement.
faqs.q: How accurate is the pixel estimate?

faqs.a: Yes. Everything runs in your browser. Nothing you type is uploaded, stored, or seen by anyone else.

serp-preview-tool.formula:
Character count = text.length

Estimated pixels:
  title px ~= characters x 8
  description px ~= characters x 7

Status rules:
  title: <= 60 chars GOOD, 61-70 WARNING, > 70 TOO LONG
  description: <= 155 chars GOOD, 156-165 WARNING, > 165 TOO LONG

Reference: Google shows roughly 600 px for titles and 920 px for descriptions.
These are estimates - real rendering depends on the letters used.

Example:
  title 'Best Coffee Shops in Mumbai | JaurTools'
  characters: 39 -> 39 x 8 = 312 px -> GOOD (<= 60, ~= 312 px of 600 px)
  description (110 chars): 110 x 7 = 770 px -> GOOD (<= 155, ~= 770 px of 920 px)
howTo: Paste or type your page title into the title box.
Watch the character count, pixel estimate, and status badge update live.
Paste or type your meta description into the description box.
Check the SERP preview to see how the snippet could look in Google.
Trim the text until both badges show green before publishing.
keyFacts: Google truncates titles at roughly 600 pixels wide - about 60 characters.
Meta descriptions truncate at roughly 920 pixels - about 155 characters.
Pixel width matters more than character count: wide letters take more room.
This tool estimates title pixels as characters x 8 and description pixels as characters x 7.
Status bands: good (green), warning (amber, close to the limit), too long (red).
The SERP preview mimics how the title and description appear in search results.

serp-preview-tool.quickAnswer: Paste your page title and meta description to check them against Google's display limits. Titles should stay under 60 characters (about 600 pixels) and descriptions under 155 characters (about 920 pixels) to avoid truncation. The tool shows live character counts, estimated pixel widths, green/amber/red status badges, and a mock search-result preview. For example, 'Best Coffee Shops in Mumbai | JaurTools' is 39 characters and about 312 pixels - safely in the green.
